newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore PCS-1 closed after two drowned.
newsitem.headline: Singapore PCS-1 closed after two drowned.

text.p: The Petrochemical Corporation of Singapore (PCS) has shutdown its first ethylene plant on Monday after two divers drowned in an industrial accident, a company official said on Tuesday.
"Yesterday afternoon two divers from a marine company on contract to PCS drowned while clearing out debris at the sea water intake pit," the official said.
The 450,000 tonne per year plant was shutdown after the accident for government officials to carry out investigations, he said.
It is unclear as to how long the plant will be closed for but the accident did not cause any damage to the units, the official said.
PCS is a 50:50 joint venture between Royal Dutch Shell and a Sumitomo Chemical led consortium of Japanese companies.
The company in April started up a new 515,000 tonne per year ethylene plant as part of a Singapore $3.4 billion expansion to the first complex.
